transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
A day after the board of chipmaker Nvidia restored Jensen Huang to the CEO's post,
Attorney General Todd Blanche sidesteped questions about any Justice Department investigation
into Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and potential export control violations.
I don't know what you're speaking about, about some export, import investigation,
but we have a lot of investigations going on.
And so, and by the way, I don't, I can't predict the future.
During a Tuesday news conference, Blanche called Nvidia a good corporate citizen
and said if Nvidia were the target of a criminal investigation,
that would not be the Trump administration's message to the public.
On Monday, President Trump said Huang had been exonerated.
However, questions from lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are swirling
after Trump took credit for Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia.
Federal investigators looking into cyberattacks against dozens of commercial shipping vessels
bound for U.S. ports and the possibility that the attacks are linked to Iran.
A U.S. official tells NPR and Iranian role strongly suspected NPR's Jenna McLaughlin reports.
In August, FBI and Coast Guard teams boarded two different vessels
to investigate intrusions into their systems and secure the ships
before they were allowed to enter U.S. ports.
But the cybersecurity threat could be much more widespread.
According to a U.S. official familiar with the matter who spoke to NPR on condition of anonymity,
the U.S. government is tracking as many as 50 foreign commercial ships,
including energy tankers, that they believe have been compromised by hackers.
The U.S. official told NPR that the bad actors took advantage of known vulnerabilities
and managed to get inside some of these ships' operational technology systems.
It could be yet another front in the U.S. war with Iran.
Jenna McLaughlin, NPR News.
The self-styled Libyan National Army says two Libyan naval officers have died from their wounds.
Following Sunday's Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship in the Libyan waters off Benghazi,
the LNA vowing to retaliate Ukraine says Sunday's attack was a legitimate act of self-defense.
Medicare Open enrollment gives 70 million people the chance to change their health insurance for the coming year.
Jackie Fortier with KFF Health News reports.
Medicare is the federal health insurance program for people 65 and older and some people with disabilities.
This year, they're facing a lot of changes.
Prescription drug costs are going up,
and millions of people on Medicare Advantage will need to pick a new plan as insurers pull out of their area.
Amy Niles is with the Patient Advocate Foundation.
This takes a little bit of time. You want time to think about what your budget might be.
Compare plans. Don't wait until the last minute.
Free help is available.
Counselors with SHIP, the state health insurance assistance program, help people on Medicare sort through their options.
Sign up for an appointment soon.
Medicare Open enrollment ends December 7th.
I'm Jackie Fortier.
This is NPR.
Maryland Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen confirming that Kilmar Abrego Garcia is leaving the country.
Van Hollen says he's traveling to a country of his choice as a free man.
Abrego Garcia is a Salvadoran migrant who became a symbol of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown
after he was wrongfully deported to a notorious El Salvador prison.
The Washington Post says he is headed to Spain as part of a negotiated deal.
House Democrats have picked up another seat, bringing their majority heading into the new Congress in January to 259.
They reached that number after the Associated Press called a Tennessee House race in favor of Democrat Victoria Broderick.
She defeated an eight-term Republican incumbent.
Ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday travel period, a group of aviation enthusiasts enjoyed a seven-course meal of airline food in Seattle.
Crystal LaGore of Oregon Public Broadcasting reports.
The sold-out event at Seattle's Museum of Flight was called the greatest airline meals of the 20th century.
And some, like Ben Morrow, came from as far away as New York to attend.
I found out about this from some online blogs, and it felt weird to not fly in for an event about airline meals.
It was the brainchild of comedy writer and food personality Bill Oakley.
The 150 attendees dined on everything from caviar to kangaroo.
Of all the courses, it was the best tasting one. I thought it was the most interesting one by far.
The event was part of a series of culinary curiosity dinners where Oakley partners with chefs around the country to create multi-course meals of unusual cuisine.
I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone, offering an alternative approach to language learning.
Moving past rote memorization, the app guides users to intuitively think in a second language using images and contextual audio, mimicking how people acquire speech as children.
The platform also includes advanced speech recognition technology that compares a learner's pronunciation directly with native speakers to refine accent precision.
Learn more about their new Rosetta Stone Sapphire app at RosettaStone.com.

topics.text: Attorney General Todd Blanche sidesteps questions on Justice Department probe of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
Federal investigators probe cyberattacks on up to 50 commercial ships bound for U.S. ports, possibly tied to Iran
Libyan National Army says two naval officers died from wounds after Ukrainian drone attack on Russian warship
Medicare open enrollment begins for 70 million people, with rising drug costs and Advantage plan changes
Senator Chris Van Hollen confirms Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaving the country for Spain under negotiated deal
House Democrats reach 259 seats for January Congress after Tennessee race call for Victoria Broderick
Seattle Museum of Flight hosts sold-out seven-course dinner of historic airline meals organized by Bill Oakley
